annotations.text:
A · CARD STACK
The standard modern iOS look.

Why: instantly familiar — big title, soft white cards on grey, one clear yellow button. Nobody has to learn it.

Trade-off: safe. It could be almost any well-made app; the MTN yellow is the only thing that says it's yours.

B · GLASS
Frosted panels over a warm colour wash.

Why: the newest-feeling of the five, and it lets the yellow fill the whole screen without shouting. Premium.

Trade-off: the busiest background — long reading is harder, and older phones render the blur less cleanly.

C · STREAK
The game comes first.

Why: opens on your streak ring and one big Play button. If the daily habit is the point, this is the one that builds it.

Trade-off: the news and the word become side dishes. It's an app you play, not one you read.

D · EDITORIAL
Dark, serif, like a good reading app.

Why: calm and grown-up. The word of the day gets the whole top of the screen, and it's kind to your eyes early and late.

Trade-off: the quietest. The quiz has to sell itself from a tab, and there's no colour to catch a bored eye.

E · WIDGETS
A board of tiles, like your phone's home screen.

Why: everything visible at a glance with no scrolling, and each tile can grow into its own feature later.

Trade-off: no single focal point — five tiles competing means nothing is obviously the main thing to do.
